fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/web -run TestWebToken shows pages without action controls and POST refused when no token is set, a POST refused with a wrong or missing token, the cookie set after a ?token= visit, and a bearer header accepted; go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run TestWebTokenSetting shows daemon.set accepts rhiza.web.token and the daemon's web handler (web_root.go) gates POSTs on the token it reads from that setting.
fields.statement: A web token (rhiza.web.token, set with rhiza daemon set and read by the daemon's web handler) turns on the web UI's actions: a browser presents it once with ?token= and keeps it in an HttpOnly cookie, a script sends it as a bearer header; without a token set, pages show no action controls and every POST is refused, and pages stay readable as today.

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/web -run 'TestWebAnswer|TestWebApprove' answers a question and approves a sign-off through POST with the token and the CSRF field, shows the confirmation, and refuses an answer or approve POST missing the CSRF field.
fields.statement: From the web UI the owner answers an open question (question.answer) and approves a sign-off (inbox.approve or run.approve), and the page then says what happened ('Answered. The run continues.').

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/web -run 'TestWebPause|TestWebActionsOnly' pauses and resumes the daemon and a project through POST with the token and the CSRF field, refuses a pause or resume POST missing the CSRF field, and gets 404 or 405 for a POST to any other path, retry, abandon and merge included.
fields.statement: From the web UI the owner pauses or resumes the daemon or one project (rhiza.daemon.paused, rhiza.project.paused), and no other action exists: every other POST path is refused.

set.statement: The daemon serves a web UI on localhost for monitoring Rhiza: the daemon, runs, the inbox and the roadmap. It is read-only except for the safe actions behind the web token (answer an inbox item, approve a sign-off, pause or resume).

The first web UI is served by the daemon process on localhost, and that first pass was read-only and for monitoring only (web-safe-actions since adds the safe actions behind the web token); the owner handles any port forwarding.

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/web -run TestWebCSRF shows action forms carry the CSRF field, a cookie-authenticated POST with the right CSRF field passes the gate, and one with a missing or wrong CSRF field is refused.
fields.statement: Every web UI POST authenticated by the token cookie must carry a CSRF field that the page's action forms include; a cookie POST with a missing or wrong CSRF field is refused, whatever action it names.
